section.sectionSummaryBrief: The maamar brings three matters, including the concept of "and He did not desire" relating to the service of tzaddikim, and explains that the advantage of teshuvah is also found in mitzvah observance, though teshuvah has two modes.
section.t: And the maamar brings the three matters,
also the concept of "and He did not desire" which is in the manner of the service of the tzaddikim,
even though the main concept of the virtue of the lower one
(Your people)
is in the service of teshuvah
(as above),
for the concept and elevation in teshuvah
(which effects change)
is also in the observance of the mitzvos
(of tzaddikim),
as brought in the maamar from the Yerushalmi: How great is the power of those who perform mitzvos.
Except that in the service of teshuvah it is in revelation.
And in teshuvah itself there are two modes,
"And He will turn... and because He loved you...,"
in each of which there is an advantage as above section 10.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The phrase "Your people, Yisrael" indicates two separate blessings—one for the simple folk and one for the learned—yet the single "bless" shows they are one, as the blessing for the simple draws from Atzmus and extends to Yisrael through internal powers.
section.t: And one may add,
that this which it says "Your people, Yisrael"
(and not "Your people and Yisrael,"
for even in this language it is emphasized that "Your people" and "Yisrael" are two matters)
is in order to hint that they are two blessings,
a blessing for Your people and a blessing for Yisrael
(as above section 2).
For in addition to this that "bless Your people" is drawn afterward through them to all Yisrael,
there is another blessing—"Yisrael."
And it may be said,
that "bless Your people,"
simple people who observe Torah and mitzvos with innocence and simplicity, is the drawing from the aspect of Atzmus
(tzemer—wool),
for the concept of simplicity is from the simplicity of the essence of the soul.
And "bless Yisrael"
(those who know Torah)
is a drawing that relates to the matter of revelations
(sheleg—snow).
And nevertheless it says "bless" one time,
in order to hint,
that they are one matter.
For "bless Your people"
is the blessing that is drawn to Yisrael,
that is,
the drawing of Atzmus into the internal powers,
so that the internal powers
(even from the aspect of their delineation)
will be according to Atzmus,
as above sections 9 and 10.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: A verse never departs from its plain meaning, and may it be speedily in our days that He bless Your people Yisrael literally, in both spiritual and physical matters.
section.t: And a verse never departs from its plain meaning,
and may it be speedily in our days, literally, "and bless Your people, Yisrael," as its plain meaning,
both in spiritual matters and in physical matters,
in children, life, and ample sustenance,
from His full, open, holy, and broad hand.
